label: Encoding-phase position ramp: original tokens from step 2 through <DEL>
explanation: Fires at almost every step from the 3rd original token (t=2) through the <DEL> step. The token at that step does not matter. Rate is 0.73 at t=2 and about 0.9-0.99 for orig_idx>=3 and at <DEL>. It is silent at t=0-1 and almost silent in the copy phase (0.6% rate, 0.2% of mass). Magnitude grows steadily over the encoding phase: top examples ramp from about 0.1 to 1.0 of max across the input, peaking on the last original tokens and <DEL>. Weakest activations are at t=2. Identity of the input, previous token and output token has no effect (lift near 1.0 across tokens). Most false positives are at t=2.

issues: The test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.904, R 0.993, F1 0.946, mass recall 0.998. Activation-quartile coverage is 0.976 to 1.000, so the misses are mostly weak activations.

The phase claims check out. Rate is 0.000 at t=0 and 0.001 at t=1, 0.730 at t=2, 0.909 to 0.989 for orig_idx 3 to 8, and 0.894 at <DEL>. The copy phase has rate 0.006 and holds 0.2% of the activation mass.

The false positives are concentrated at t=2: about 135k of the 263k false positives on dev. The rest are scattered silent <DEL> steps (rate 0.89), whose rate does not depend on L (0.92 for L<=4, 0.86 for L>=7).

The claim that the token has no effect is slightly overstated at t=2. Precision there is 0.64 when the previous token equals the first token, 0.67 when the input is a digit and 0.82 when the previous token is a digit, against 0.73 overall. The effect is mild and does not make a usable predicate. Over the full window, n_digits makes no difference (precision 0.909 vs 0.900).

The magnitude claim is roughly right. Mean mass per active step rises from orig_idx 2 to about 6-7, then flattens and dips slightly at orig_idx 8-9. <DEL> is close to the peak. It is not a strict ramp to <DEL>, but 'peaking on the last original tokens and <DEL>' is acceptable.
The misses on the test split are weak, scattered copy-phase activations at various recall_idx values. There is no systematic class. I found no better predicate.
